subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.

spec.name: Calder Hanging Mobile
spec.description: A Calder-style kinetic mobile: a ceiling hook and wire hang a balanced tree of black rods, each ending in a flat painted organic shape in primary colours.
spec.layout: A hanging piece that keeps its height: its lowest shape hangs about 0.15 m above y = 0, and the ceiling hook sits at the top at y = 2.2. From the hook a thin black wire drops to the main rod at y 1.75, which runs about 1.2 m along X. On the +X end a thin wire drops to a medium rod (y 1.3) that carries a big red leaf and a small black disc. On the -X end a wire drops to a rod (y 1.45) that carries a blue kidney shape on a long wire and a sub-rod holding yellow and white discs. A centre wire from the main rod drops to a third rod at y 0.9, set rotated 40 degrees in Z-depth, with a black teardrop and a red circle. All shapes are thin extrusions (about 0.012 m thick) with flat colour and a slight tilt for hand-cut character. Rods are thin black capsules with small round loops and tiny hooks at each wire joint. Shapes are spread in X and Z (depth up to 0.6 m) so the silhouette reads from every side. Matte primary palette with black and white accents. Nothing touches the floor.

parts.builds: Ceiling hook, small ceiling plate disc, the wire down to the main rod, the main black rod with end loops, and the three drop wires from its right end, left end and centre, each with small hook loops. Also a small counterweight black ball at the main rod's right end.
parts.attaches: Starts at mount hook; drop wires end at rodRight, rodLeft and rodLow mounts.

parts.builds: Rod at rodRight (about 0.9 m long, black), its wires, a large red leaf-shaped extrusion hanging on a wire from the rod's far end, a small black disc on the near end, plus a tiny white circle accent painted on the red leaf. Shapes tilted slightly.
parts.attaches: Hangs from the topAssembly wire at mount rodRight.

parts.builds: Rod at rodLeft, a blue kidney-shaped extrusion on a long wire, a sub-rod at subRodLeft carrying a yellow disc and a white disc on different wire lengths, small black loops at junctions.
parts.attaches: Hangs from the topAssembly wire at mount rodLeft.

parts.builds: Rod at rodLow turned 40 degrees about Y, a black teardrop shape on one end, a red circle with a yellow centre dot on a wire at the other, and a small white crescent hanging from the centre of the rod on a short wire.
parts.attaches: Hangs from the topAssembly centre wire at mount rodLow.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a static assembly with no joints, using the given context to place parts by coordinates—starting with a ceiling plate modeled as a small cylinder near the top of the bounding box.

Below it I'm hanging a hook made of a small torus ring with a stem, then a wire connecting down to a horizontal main rod spanning roughly ±0.6 along X at mid-height, with additional mounting points branching off to secondary rods at slightly offset positions. I'm using thin capsule shapes for wires and slightly thicker ones for rods, letting some wires slant a bit in Z to reach their mounts since the offsets stay reasonably close to the bounding box.

Adding ring loops at the rod ends...

Finalizing the hook as a small torus arc, then adding crimp sleeves at wire tops and figuring out the counterweight ball placement at the main rod's right end, aligning rod length and ball radius so it caps cleanly around x=0.6-0.63.

Now I'm detailing both ends of the rod - a small collar/cap bead on the left end, and the center loop where the rod hangs from the top wire, with a separate drop wire looping below the rod center. I'm also planning small finishing touches like a ceiling plate with rim screws and a canopy cover.

I'm lathing a dome-shaped canopy profile for the ceiling plate, positioning it at the top and adding small screw spheres around its rim.

Now I'm adding a hanging assembly below it: a stem, then interlocked swivel rings (one in the XY plane, one rotated into YZ) to simulate a chain link, finishing with the wire starting point near y=2.025.

I'm setting up helper functions for drawing wire segments and rods with consistent radius and color, defining the part geometry calls I'll need for the mid-wire details.

Adding ferrule bands and loop rings...

Simpler approach: a collar band on the rod with torus eyes on top and bottom for the wires to attach to, then a small arc-shaped hook torus at the mount point where the wire terminates.

Adding counterweight sphere...

I'm working out the buildRightBranch function, planning to mount the rod at roughly [0.55, 1.3, 0.1] with a bounding box spanning x 0.2–1.3, y 0.4–1.35, z -0.3–0.5, using the Ctx type as given without importing it.

I'm computing the rod's geometry with a near end holding a small black disc and a far end with a longer arm for the big red leaf, keeping it slightly tilted along Y for depth, and planning small loop/torus elements at the pivot and far end to connect the hanging wires within the box bounds.

For the leaf shape, I'm sketching an asymmetric outline in the XY plane that tapers from a top attachment point down to a tip, then extruding it with thin thickness along Z and tilting it about Y so it reads naturally from the sides.

Still computing rod and leaf positions...

Adding midrib and vein rods across both leaf faces...

Placing small eyelets at the leaf top and rod end for the wire to pass through, then adding a torus collar ring oriented around the rod's axis at its far end to form a hanging loop.

I'll add a second interlinked ring above the pivot collar, checking its height stays under the 1.35 ceiling, then connect it with a short vertical wire stub up to the mount point for a clean finish.

For the near end, I'm hanging a tilted black disc from a short wire drop — positioning its center using the wire length and tilt angle, orienting it to face roughly along z, and giving it a tiny white pinhole dot in the center for detail against the dark "#1a1a1a" material.

Now I'm adding small sphere caps at the rod ends for a balanced counterweight look, with the rod itself rendered as a rounded capsule connecting near and far points, and I'm attaching a tiny eyelet torus ring at the top of the disc where the wire connects.

For the rod orientation I'm computing the direction vector between endpoints and using it to set collar ring orientation, with a second perpendicular ring that interlinks correctly with the collar. For the leaf shape I'm working out the yaw tilt so the outline leans toward the z-axis at a 35-degree angle.

I want the leaf's secondary axis to stay orthogonal to its tilted x-axis, so I'm projecting out the shared component and renormalizing with a vector library rather than assuming an approximate roll will work. I'm also checking the leaf outline for smoothness, noting the stem and tip points need sharper corners.

Laying out the leaf outline points and verifying they trace a convex-ish shape without self-intersection, with the leaf height around 0.5 adjusted for tilt so it still sits above the box minimum. Now I'm figuring out where to place the eyelet ring relative to the leaf's attachment point.

I'm deciding to skip a stem notch and secondary outline layer to keep part count low, instead adding a few darker red veins radiating down the leaf for detail rather than extra geometry.

Calculating vein endpoints...

Still writing geometry code...

I'm weighing whether to treat Ctx as an externally-provided type or just declare it loosely as any, since redeclaring it risks conflicting with the module's own definition if the code gets concatenated together.

Now I'm working out the rod geometry for the low assembly—positioning it at a 40° rotation about Y, computing its endpoints so they stay within the bounding box, and planning the hanging shapes (teardrop, red circle, crescent) along with a small loop and hook at the center mount point. I'm calculating exact coordinates for where each shape attaches to the rod and wire.

I'm positioning the crescent near the rod's center while the teardrop and circle sit at the ends, and varying each shape's facing direction so the teardrop rotates diagonally, the circle faces along the rod for contrast, and the crescent aligns with the drawing plane.

Now I'm working out how to orient the extruded outlines at each attachment point—setting the teardrop's origin at its tip with a slight tilt, and figuring out how to compute a perpendicular x-axis so the shape's plane stays roughly orthogonal even with the tilt applied.

Working out the dot decal placement — using a slightly thicker yellow circle layered over the red circle, centered at the top attach point offset by the radius, so it reads as a centered dot on the face.

Now I'm sketching the teardrop outline as a 14-16 point polygon: a sharp tip at the top transitioning into a rounded bulb below, computing the tangent angles where the straight tip lines meet the bulb's circular arc so the curve stays smooth.

I'm working out the bulb's bottom position and smoothing its tip, placing roughly ten points around the curve. Now I'm moving on to designing a crescent shape—an outer arc and inner arc forming the moon outline—and figuring out how to hang it by a wire attached near its outer edge so the tips angle upward like a bowl.

Working out where the inner circle's tips need to meet the outer arc endpoints so the crescent shape closes properly, solving for the inner circle's center offset and radius so both arcs intersect at the same tip points.

Working through this more carefully, I realize the inner arc that's actually inside the outer disc is the left portion, bulging from the upper tip through 180° to the lower tip. So the crescent boundary traces: outer arc from the upper tip through the left side to the lower tip, then back along the inner arc from the lower tip through 180° to the upper tip, closing the shape.

Now I'm figuring out the attachment points — the wire hangs from the top of the outer circle (at ψ=90°), and I want small decorative elements like tiny torus loops and hooks at the rod ends and where the wire meets the crescent shape, to give it a finished, jewelry-like look with a gap facing right.

For the hook detail I'll use a small arc torus to form an eyelet with an open hook shape, keeping it simple rather than fully modeling a clasp. Rod ends get small black sphere caps for that Calder-style finish, with the rod itself a thin capsule, and I'll add a center loop above the rod plus a small hook arc near the top.

Below the rod center I'm hanging a crescent wire shape, positioned so it doesn't collide with the teardrop and circle elements at the rod ends since they're spaced far enough apart. To match the red circle with yellow dot and white crescent spec, I'm considering adding a small white accent dot on the black teardrop to round out the color palette.

I'm working out wire lengths and positions for the red circle and teardrop so everything stays within the bounding box, checking their vertical extents and z-depth given the rod's rotation angle.

Now I'm setting the yaw angles for each shape relative to the rod direction, then writing the extrude code to attach the teardrop's eyelet ring and connecting wire at the correct offset from its tip.

I'm applying a small Euler tilt to the shape's local axes for a slight rotation while keeping the attachment point fixed at the tip, then computing the circle's center and outline points relative to that top point.

For the teardrop, I'll add a small white dot near the bulb center for detail, skipping an extra accent on the red circle since that's handled by the other branch. Then I'll finalize the code.

I'm figuring out how to type the Ctx parameter for buildLeftBranch without importing the module's own type, considering whether a local type alias with loose typing would work safely.

Now I'm working out the actual geometry for rodLeft's position and the rod's endpoints so the suspension wire from the top assembly connects properly to the mount point, nudging the x-coordinates to keep it within the bounding box.

I'm planning the layout: the rod runs between two slightly offset endpoints with a small eyelet ring at the mount, and a wire extends down from the rod's other end toward the blue kidney shape positioned lower in the box.

Now I'm working out positioning so the kidney doesn't exceed the box bounds, weighing whether it should attach further left on the rod and adjusting its centering relative to the mount point.

I'm working out the kidney shape's hang point and vertical wire connecting it to the rod end, adjusting its yaw and center position so it fits within bounds, then shifting focus to the lowest extent of the box and positioning the sub-rod discs below.

I'll keep the rod spanning -0.98 to -0.22 and work out the sub-rod's yawed endpoints, computing A and B positions from the center with a 30° rotation. Then I'm hanging a yellow disc from end A with a short wire and a white disc from end B with a longer one.

I'll angle the disc with some yaw so its x-extent shrinks a bit, keeping it within the box bounds, and shift the sub-rod mount closer to center at -0.95 to adjust the wire geometry connecting the rod end to the sub-rod.

With those constants settled, I'm now building a kidney-shaped outline through an extrude helper that takes the outline points, position, direction vectors, thickness, and bevel, defining the shape in local coordinates relative to its hang point so it drapes downward correctly.

For orientation, I'll use a quaternion built from yaw and tilt rotations to derive orthonormal x and y basis vectors, ensuring the shape stays properly aligned even with the swing tilt, then attach the outline's top to the hang point with an eyelet there.

I'm shaping the kidney outline with a bean-curve formula using a modulated radius that pinches inward near the top to form a notch, then shifting the whole shape down so that notch point aligns with the hang point.

I'll place the eyelet wire right at the notch edge, use about 24 points for a low-poly but non-crossing star-shaped outline, and consider a slight 3D tilt rather than rotating in 2D. For detail, I'm thinking of adding a subtle inner color inset or small dot within the limited six-color palette, since the geometry itself should carry most of the visual character.

Keeping decorations minimal and Calder-like, I'll add a tiny white dot on the kidney shape and a small blue dot on the yellow disc, offsetting them slightly outward along the surface normal using the local basis vectors so they sit just above the front face.

I'm writing a helper function for stamping outlined shapes with optional dots onto both faces, building circular outlines as 20-sided polygons with a slight hand-cut wobble for the yellow disc, and defining the wire rods using capsule shapes with black color for the main rods and a distinct wire color for the thinner connectors.

For the loop joints at rod ends, I'm placing small toruses oriented so the ring wraps around the rod tip like an eyelet, offsetting them slightly inward from the ends.

Now I'm working out the hook detail where the wire attaches: a small torus hanging below the loop, positioned at the rod's end point and offset downward, with the wire running from that point further down.

Still working out hook geometry...

Mapping out where the mount wire overlaps the hook stub, I decide it's fine to let the small overlap stand. For the sub-rod assembly, I'm placing a top wire connecting the rod end to the sub-rod center with a collar and hook, keeping the z-depth consistent at -0.1, then moving on to figure out the rod's right end with its wrapped ring and hook below.

I'm checking the kidney shape's yaw angle against the box boundary—at 55° it extends slightly past the edge, so I adjust to 65° yaw with the rod's right end pulled in to x=-0.27 to keep everything contained.

Now I'm working out the vertical hang position: tracing the wire down to the ring, then calculating where the kidney's lobes and notch sit relative to the hang point so the shape reads correctly without overlapping other elements.

Now I'm sizing the yellow and white discs, positioning them so they hang from the ring at top, and adding slight wobble and yaw rotations to each so their faces read correctly in the attachment view.

I'm considering adding small wrap rings or hooks at the rod ends and center, plus tiny decorative details on the kidney shape like a small white circle, though I'll keep most of these minimal. I'm also setting a slight tilt on the shapes using small X and Z rotation offsets alongside the yaw.

For the hanging rings, I'm working out the orientation math so the ring's torus normal aligns properly with its attachment direction using quaternions, and for the small dots I'm positioning them along the surface with a slight offset so they sit flush on the face.

Now I'm thinking through smoothing and bevel settings, confirming bevel radius works with the thickness and circle resolution, and sketching out which palette colors pair with which pieces -- white dots on blue, black on white, and so on.

For the rod function, I'm deciding not to pass a bone parameter since there are no joints in this model, and setting sweep resolution to fewer sides for wire-like rods versus more sides for thicker capsule rods. I'm also working out how to orient a collar torus or hook ring around a rod by computing its normal from the rod direction crossed with an up vector.

Writing hook geometry code...

Setting up a hanging-shape helper with orientation and dot-placement logic for decorative circles along the shape's surface, plus an outline generator for custom circle shapes with randomized wobble.

For the kidney shape I'm working out a star-shaped polar curve with a notch at the top to avoid self-crossing, pushing the lobes outward and shifting the center so points stay ordered counter-clockwise for extrusion.

I'm also adding small decorative black spheres as terminal beads at the rod ends, and working out how to form the mounting loop above the rod so it hooks upward into the collar rather than hanging downward.

I need a helper for the collar-and-loop wire connection around the sub-rod, similar to the mount loop, returning the top point of the loop so the wire can attach there. Then I'm setting hook directions for each rod end and working out the sub-rod's orientation using the yaw angle.

Now I'm computing the left branch's rod and kidney positions, checking the hook and eyelet coordinates line up, and verifying the wire length between them comes out to about 0.88 meters as intended.

Interpolating the mount position along the rod and setting sub-component centers with offsets for the kidney and collar pieces. Now I'm working out the final coordinate math before writing the actual builder code with proper types for the context object.

Writing branch-builder functions...
